text.tspan: JOEYY - SHARED BACKEND (BUSINESS APP + CUSTOMER APP) - REQUEST FLOWS + DATA MODEL
Evolved from the agreed Partner MVP diagram: same sign-in -> authenticated route -> handler -> database flow, now serving both apps, NFC readers, and Apple Wallet.
Read left to right: caller -> API routes -> handler -> database. Highlighted handlers and tables are SHARED: written by one app, read by both.
API verifies signature / issuer / audience / expiry
using the provider's keys (no extra auth service)
ONE BACKEND APPLICATION - handlers are logical modules, NOT separate services
DEVICES (EXTERNAL - NFC NEVER WRITES TO THE DB)
punch on full card -> NEW card
Push: pass updated / new card started / rewards waiting (also to the business app)
One per completed card; rewards stack
id (PK), businessId, kind, payload, createdAt, readAt
Full card (e.g. 10/10) stays full; reward earned.
Next punch -> NEW card with punches = 1.
No claim or redemption required; rewards stack.
Business is notified: new card + reward waiting.
Example: v1 = 10, v2 = 8. Card A (v1) still
needs 10; new and rollover cards use v2.
Apps pick periods in business time zone;
BOUNDARIES: one business + one active program per owner. No POS, employee roles, campaigns, or manual punch authorization. NFC readers never write to the database directly.
